subject: welding
intro: Welding leads into the fabrication shops, building sites and inspection labs where metal is joined — the people who run the arc, cut and fit the joints, and certify that the weld will hold.

roles.title: Welders, Cutters, Solderers, and Brazers
roles.what: Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, soldering and brazing equipment to join metal components or fill holes, indentations and seams in fabricated metal products, in shops and on site.
roles.where: Units 2 to 5 are the job itself: SMAW stick, GMAW and FCAW wire processes, TIG on stainless and aluminium, plus oxy-fuel and plasma cutting and joint preparation and fit-up.

roles.title: Sheet Metal Workers
roles.what: Fabricate, assemble, install and repair sheet metal products — ducts, drainpipes, casings — cutting, bending and shaping metal and welding or soldering parts, then smoothing and checking the seams.
roles.where: Unit 5's cutting, joint preparation and fit-up and unit 3's MIG practice on thin and aluminium stock are exactly the joining work sheet metal ducts demand.

roles.title: Structural Iron and Steel Workers
roles.what: Install structural and reinforcing iron and steel to form and support buildings, bridges and other structures, aligning the steel and welding or bolting the connections that carry the load.
roles.where: Unit 6's weld defects, symbols and codes, WPS and inspection govern structural connections, while unit 1's arc, fume and fire hazards set the site-safety discipline.

roles.title: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
roles.what: Inspect, test and sort raw materials, parts and fabricated products for defects and deviations from specification, using precision measuring instruments and test equipment.
roles.where: Unit 6's metallurgy, heat-affected zones, weld defects and symbols, and codes, WPS and inspection make you the person who judges whether a weld passes.
